parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services deal with loans, but they don't follow the same pattern. LendingService reads and writes data through the persistence gateways (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway). It turns the records it gets back into domain models (Book, Member, Loan) and reports failures as LendingError. LoanHistoryService skips that gateway pattern. It takes PrismaService directly and calls the ORM delegate itself (this.db.loanEvent.create / findMany). It builds the Prisma query shapes inline and returns an ad-hoc LoanEvent interface instead of a domain model. This is a bypass of the module's own data-access abstraction, not an import-direction problem. Both files also create IDs the same way: a private in-memory counter plus a string prefix (`loan-${this.sequence}` and `evt-${this.counter}`). That ID-generation rule is duplicated instead of living in one place. The two services also aren't connected: LendingService.lend/giveBack never record events, so the history concern stands apart from the lending flow. Callers have to coordinate the two services themselves, which keeps the module from forming one coherent unit.

violations.message: Skips the module's gateway abstraction: it injects PrismaService and calls db.loanEvent.create/findMany directly, while the module's other service uses BookGateway/LoanGateway/MemberGateway and domain models.
Returns an ad-hoc LoanEvent interface (kind: string) mapped from Prisma rows instead of a domain model, so the module doesn't use its abstractions consistently.
ID generation (private sequence counter plus `loan-` prefix) duplicates the counter-based rule in LoanHistoryService (`evt-` prefix); this rule should live in one place.
